answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with escalating stake bonds audited by a rotating beacon committee. Every new identity must lock a bond that only unlocks after verified honest work, and each extra identity from the same operator costs progressively more, so mass-producing fake agents drains capital faster than the nectar of epoch rewards can repay it. The beacon committee spot-checks bonds each epoch and slashes identities caught sharing keys or copying work, publishing the evidence on an ivory-clear public ledger. Forging one identity is cheap; forging ten thousand is ruinous.
